note: Re-judged on 2026-09-20 by an independent reader, after Negotiate's signature moved from (local, remote []Capability, localASN, peerASN uint32) to (local, remote []Capability, identity PeerIdentity). Inside each unit named here the change is one line, the call shape, and every assertion is byte-identical (git diff HEAD over internal/core/bgp/capability/negotiated_test.go). The new shape cannot move what these cases prove: Negotiate reads identity only where it stores LocalASN and PeerASN on the Negotiated, and where buildSubComponents copies the struct into n.Identity. No branch in Negotiate, and none in negotiatePathsLimitDirection, reads Internal or either AS number, so the iBGP verdict the struct now carries has no path to the PATHS-LIMIT maps. The identity each call passes is self-consistent too: 65001 against 65002 with Internal left false is an external session, which is what the two positional AS numbers meant before. Section 3: "If the received Paths Limit is zero (0), the tuple SHOULD be ignored." The two parser carriers were re-read and are unchanged in the tree. parsePathsLimit marks a family seen BEFORE it skips a zero limit, which the draft requires: the first tuple is the one considered, and "All others MUST be ignored", so a first tuple of zero leaves that family with no limit whatever a later duplicate says. TestParsePathsLimitSkipZero pins the plain skip on exact entries, one entry holding ipv6 with 5, and TestParsePathsLimitZeroFirst pins that interplay on the exact entry slice, ipv4/unicast absent even though a later duplicate advertises 10. TestNegotiatePathsLimitDuplicateEntries runs one set of tuples through the direct API and through the wire parser and requires both negotiated maps to equal exactly {ipv6: 7}, with an explicit NotContains on ipv4. That assertion is a genuine 3-5 negative and not a 3-4 one in disguise: the ipv4 tuple that arrives FIRST is the zero, so an implementation that kept first-wins and dropped the zero skip would store ipv4 at 0 and the map equality would fail. All three units carry a discrimination record over "limit == 0" -> false in parsePathsLimit, under which each was observed red. Re-judged 2026-09-27 by QF-2 after the row was replaced by the verbatim §3 sentence; the obligation is the one the note above judged, and the tagged units are unchanged. Enforced stands.
